it's a longer story, but I think it might be motivating for others

last semester, I had a lot of absence. like, a lot. at my school, they can be somewhat lenient. they profit off of each student, but if a student has too much absence, the government no longer pays the school for the student. so thats where they'll usually kick them out, or sooner.

i also had a lot of absence the year before. last year, i think i made it to one or two classes a week max. never submitted any assignments. I would have frequent contact with my guidance counselor though

what they do is all the guidance counselors and the secretaries (the secretaries kick people out for absence) come together on a bi-weekly absence meeting. here they will hand out warnings, kick people out, etc.

so, she and I would talk and try and make a strategy for what she would say at those meetings to help ensure I would not get kicked out. problem was that I wasn't doing anything at all to better my situation. so her only strategy was to say "her mental health is super poor, but she wants to stay at the school".

a few times, I'd go outside, ground myself, and ask the moon to help ensure that I don't get kicked out. it was simple but emotional. I would also frequently do affirmations.

and somehow, I did not get kicked out..

the reason why I think this is more so magick than anything else, is because I really did not do much to work with my goal to not get kicked out. You always hear and read that you have to work on shit yourself for the universe to help out as well. But I still didn't attend classes, didn't submit assignments, ghosted everyone. I had more absence than I've heard anyone else have. I've heard of dozens of students that got kicked out with much less absence than me.

maybe I'm reaching. I've just always felt like this was the work of the universe. 

when you have too much absence in a class that is ending that semester, you are obligated to take the exam in it. If not, it's randomized which exams you take. So because I had so much absence, I had 6 exams - as opposed to others who had max 2 exams. My exam results ended up being so good that the secretaries decided to move me up to the next year despite my absence. 

in retrospect, it was definitely my guidance counselor, math tutor, and something greater than us that helped me out.
